# Summary of run on issue #449

## The work

Issue **#449** (labels: bug, `atomaton/in-progress`) asks for a fix: a merged PR stays permanently readable as "running" because the post-merge handoff is written onto the PR's own thread as `atomaton:ended=handoff`. The owner (`@yuma-seno`) fixed the policy as **提案1**: separate `handoff` (this node is held by an agent) from `chain_continues` (a run started somewhere, so "nothing runs next" is not true). The issue is one engineer-ready leaf; `/engineer recover` was the last command, so prior sessions are archived and this session is a rebuild.

**Owner's scope (must be honoured):**
1. A post-merge parent dispatch must **not** make the PR's result comment `ended=handoff`; the PR run's own conclusion (`done`) becomes the tag. A directive naming the next agent **on THIS node** still produces `handed-off`.
2. "A run started right after" is a **separate signal**; the ops-log `dispatch` op and the runner's `chain_continues` output must **not** change (`shouldReleaseGuard` and the aggregation double signal read them). The mention-suppressing intent of `chain_continues` must be preserved.
3. Readers must treat existing data: a **merged PR** with an old `ended=handoff` returns `runInFlight` false. **Restrict to merged PRs only** — do not degrade genuinely running issues or unmerged/closed PRs.
4. `stop_on_close`'s root notice may say "an agent was working on it" only when the root itself has a run in flight; closing a parent containing only merged PRs produces neither "Runs were going on ..." nor `stop=requested`.
5. Tests must pin: merged-PR handoff not in flight, close of parent with merged PR silent, root notice wording, and that genuinely running work is still stopped — using the fake `gh`.
6. **No version bump** in `package.json`. Changes only under `src/**`; `.github/**` is generated. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` must exit 0.
7. Existing tests pinning the wrong behaviour must be updated deliberately: `mcp.test.ts:2352`, `turn.test.ts:113-114`, `completion-mention.test.ts:147`.

## Design decided (and implemented as described)

`chainContinues` alone no longer produces `handed-off`. `TurnEnding` gained `continues?: true`; `endingOf` returns `finished`/`no-report` plus `continues` when a dispatch went elsewhere, and still returns `handed-off` when a directive is present. `shouldReleaseGuard` returns false for `continues` (label behaviour unchanged, deliberately). `completion-mention.ts` suppresses on `chainContinues || ending.continues`, and the `chainContinues` check moved **above** the `no-report` override so a silent chain-continuing run no longer mentions a person. Readers narrowed at `runInFlight(repo, number, { merged })`: merged ⇒ only `shaped.holder === "agent"` counts, so the run that performs its own merge is still in flight. `work-tree.ts`'s `runningOn(repo, number, merged)` now takes the flag; all three call sites pass it (`readNode` derives it from `pull_request.merged_at`, `readChildren`'s PR search from `state === "MERGED"`, the native-links children pass `false`). `stopOnCloseNotice(number, running)` has two receipts; `stopOnCloseBody` became an options object `{ number, rootRunning, closed, stopped }` that writes `STOP_TAG` only when the root is running. `stop_on_close.ts` computes `rootRunning` from the subtree and passes descendants only as `stopped`.

## Done

Edits complete in: `src/domain/work/turn.ts` (Ending doc, `TurnEnding.continues`, `endingOf`, `shouldReleaseGuard`), `src/domain/work/completion-mention.ts` (ordering + `ending.continues` + doc), `src/adapters/github/thread.ts` (`runInFlight` options + doc), `src/adapters/github/work-tree.ts` (`runningOn` signature + 3 call sites), `src/domain/work/closed-target.ts` (`stopOnCloseNotice(number, running)`), `src/entrypoints/machinery/stop_on_close.ts` (body signature + `rootRunning`).

Tests updated/added: `turn.test.ts` (handoff-vs-continues cases, guard arm, dispatch-nothing), `completion-mention.test.ts` (explicit silencing tests), `closed-target.test.ts` (idle-root receipt), `thread.test.ts` (`inFlight` helper takes options; `describe("on a merged pull request")` with 4 cases + closed-issue case — all 13 pass), and `stop_on_close.test.ts` (`MERGED_PR_HANDOFF_THREAD` fixture, `describe("closing a parent whose only children are merged pull requests")` with two cases, plus an "idle root and a running child" test) — **this last file has NOT yet been run**.

Clean at last check: `bun run typecheck` exit 0; `bun test ./src/domain ./src/adapters` → 968 pass, 0 fail. `bun run synth` leaves the tree clean (no `.github/**` diff).

## Still open

1. **Run `bun test src/entrypoints/machinery/stop_on_close.test.ts`** — the new tests are unverified; `subIssues({number: 807})` with an OPEN child must still let `nodesToClose` see it, and the "not toContain `Runs were going on`" cases may need fixture adjustment.
2. **`decide_turn_ending.ts`** — not yet touched: `ends` output unchanged, but `published` needs no change since `continues` does not add an output. Consider whether `ended` being `finished` instead of `handed-off` for a chain-continuing run is visible anywhere in the runner; verified no workflow step reads `turn-ending.ended`, so no `.wac.ts` change is needed.
3. **`post_result_comment.ts`** — `endingHere`/`endedTag` now yield `done` for a chain-continuing run automatically (exhaustive switch unchanged). `post_result_comment.test.ts:198` ("omits the mention when the chain already continues") should still pass; confirm, and consider adding an assertion that the tag is `done` not `handoff` for that case.
4. **`mcp.test.ts:2352`** — the merge_pr test asserts only the ops-log `op: dispatch`, which is still correct; the docstring says the result comment claims "No agent will be automatically executed next" — the test does not assert the comment. Leave the ops-log assertion, update the comment's wording if the run reads it.
5. **`dispatch.test.ts:99`** — passes unchanged (ops-log classification untouched).
6. **`decide_turn_ending.test.ts:35-37`** — "stays held when the chain already continues" still passes; may want an added assertion that `ended` is now `finished`.
7. Run the full `bun test` (must exit 0), then `commit_and_push` and `create_pr(..., reviewer="reviewer")`, reading `validation_dispatched`.
8. Optional: `docs/work/how-it-works/what-keeps-two-runs-off-one-issue.md:18` describes `ended=handoff` as holding the thread open — the doc is accurate for a directive handoff and still true; no edit strictly required.

## Must not redo / must not forget

- Do not re-read `turn.ts`, `thread.ts` (both), `closed-target.ts`, `stop_on_close.ts`, `work-tree.ts` (both), `dispatch-targets.ts`, `post_result_comment.ts`, `ops-log.ts`, `dispatch.ts` — the map and decisions above are the product.
- Do not edit `.github/workflows/**` or `.github/atomaton-runtime/**`; do not bump `package.json` version; do not change ops-log op names or the runner's `chain_continues` output.

- `stopOnCloseBody`'s signature changed; it has no test calling it directly (only via the script), but any future caller must use the options object.
- A degraded delegate tool report (`free_quota_exhausted`, 402) should be filed with `create_root_issue` if it recurs in a load-bearing way.

# Skill: project/conventions

# Repository conventions

This repository builds Atomaton, the delivery template. It is both the producer of
that template and an adopter of it, which creates rules that do not apply
anywhere else.

This file is not part of the template. Its source is `self/atomaton/skills/project/`,
and it is deliberately absent from `src/` so adopters never receive it.

## The four trees

| Tree | What it is | Who writes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/**` | Source of the deliverable | You |
| `dist/.github/**` | The deliverable adopters receive | The build |
| `self/**` | This repository's own files, the ones that are not the template's | You |
| `.github/**` | This repository's running configuration | The self-deploy job, from a release plus `self/` |

Two different activities live in this table, and which one you are doing decides
which rules apply:

- **improving the deliverable** — `src/**`. It affects every adopter, and it
  reaches this repository only after a release and a self-deploy.
- **improving this repository's own operation** — `self/**`. It affects nobody
  else, and it applies as soon as it merges.

The rest of this file does not separate them cleanly. That is a known gap, tracked
in the documentation restructure; until then, read each rule and ask which of the two it is about.

`src/content/**` is mirrored verbatim into `dist/.github/atomaton/` and from there
into an adopter's repository. **It may only contain content that holds for any
project using Atomaton.** No reference to this repository's build pipeline, no
mention of `dist/`, `bun run synth`, or `build-dist.ts`, and no incident history
or PR numbers. If a rule is about developing *this* repository, it belongs in
this file instead.

## Generated output is not tracked

Change `src/**` only. `dist/**` is gitignored, so there is nothing generated to
commit and nothing to keep in sync.

Run `bun run synth` freely to inspect what adopters would receive. It writes only
into the ignored `dist/`, so it cannot dirty your commit.

Adopters receive the deliverable from a release, not from a merge, so nothing you
merge needs to carry it.

**Never touch `version` in `package.json`.** The version is the release declaration:
merging an edit to it publishes to adopters, and that decision belongs to a person,
made on the pull request the **Atomaton Release** workflow opens — never inside a
work pull request. A version left alone is a merge that publishes nothing, which is
the normal case. A work pull request that arrives with a version change in it is a
merge-blocking defect: flag it, and have the edit taken back out before merge.

`.github/**` is a different matter — see below. It is tracked, and every file in it
comes from either the release or `self/`.

## main is protected; everything lands by pull request

`.github/atomaton/rulesets/main.json` is the source of truth for what may reach main:
direct pushes are refused, and a pull request cannot merge until the `check` job
passes. It is applied by hand from an account with admin, and taken as correctly
configured thereafter — nothing verifies it, because a check could only report and
never enforce: with no ruleset, `check` would not be a required context either.

Changing the rule is a pull request against the JSON, followed by one `gh api`
call from an account with admin (see CONTRIBUTING.md). CI cannot make that call —
`administration` is not a permission a workflow can hold.

`check_merge_readiness` reports against whatever the ruleset currently
requires, so it follows the file rather than holding a second opinion.

Nothing bypasses it. No workflow writes to main — the release job attaches the deliverable
to a release instead — and your merge satisfies the rules like anyone else's. Do
not propose a bypass actor: it would mean naming a GitHub App ID or a deploy key,
values that exist only after manual setup, so the JSON would stop describing the
whole configuration.

The workflows that run agents are generated from `src/workflows/` and shipped.
`self/workflows/` holds the two that are not: `atomaton-self-deploy.yml` and
`probe-dumpable.yml`.

## Adding a static file to the deliverable

A new non-code file under `src/content/` must also be added to `build-dist.ts`'s
verbatim-copy list, or it never reaches `dist/` at all.
`tests/contract/deployment-contract.test.ts` enforces this.

## `atoma validate` is on the CLI

The `atoma` binary is on the agent's PATH — the runner installs it at
`/usr/local/bin/atoma` — and it has a `validate` subcommand that checks an agent
definition against a tools file without starting a run:

```bash
atoma validate --agent-def .github/atomaton/agent-definitions/engineer.md \
               --tools-file /tmp/tools.yaml
```

It resolves every name in the definition's `mcp_servers` against the tools file,
checks the template's placeholders, and reports what it finds. `atomaton-validate-pr`

# Skill: delivery/pipeline-setup

# Setting up verification and deployment

Read this when `checks` in `.github/atomaton/config.yaml` is empty, when a pull
request comes back with no required check on it, or when nothing deploys on merge
and the work in front of you needs one of those. Not a procedure to follow on
request — a description of how this is arranged here, because the obvious approach
does not work.

## You cannot write a workflow. You do not need to.

`GITHUB_TOKEN` is refused a write under `.github/workflows/**`. Measured where this
was written: by identity rather than by a rule someone set, on every path and
branch tried, through `git push` and through the API alike, and with no permission
in the token's own set that grants it.

**What would show this has changed is a workflow write that is ACCEPTED**, or a
refusal whose own words name a permission the token could be granted. Neither is
an answer you are hoping for, so this is not a question to put to the endpoint:
make the change the paragraph implies. Everything a pipeline actually *does* is a
command, and a command goes in `.github/atomaton/config.yaml`, which you can write
— two workflows that already ship run them. The expected refusal is confirmation
rather than news: if one does arrive, quote its own words in your report and stop.
Do not retry it as another token, another request shape or another branch, and do
not ask a person to paste a workflow file in its place — a pipeline outside the
reviewed path is what the refusal exists to prevent, and the file you can write
already does the job.

## The environment

What the project needs *installed* is separate from what verifies it:

```yaml
environment:
  setup_commands:
    - bun install --frozen-lockfile
```

Write it here once and every job runs it: the agent's own shell, the checks, and
the deployment. That is the point of the separate block. Putting `bun install` at
the front of a `checks.from_pull_request` entry instead looks equivalent and is not —
the agent's shell then has the dependencies and CI installs them again, or the
reverse, and the two environments drift. A test that passes for the agent and
fails in CI comes back to an engineer as a defect that does not reproduce.

System packages belong here too, and only here. An agent cannot install one during
a run.

## Verification

`checks` has two arms and takes exactly one. Fill in Atomaton's lists and the shipped
workflow runs your commands:

```yaml
checks:
  from_pull_request:
    - name: verify
      commands:
        - bun run typecheck
        - bun test
```

Each entry becomes one job in `atomaton-check.yml`, running after the environment setup
above; its commands run in order and the first failure ends that job.
Whatever a contributor would type to check the project locally is what belongs
here — read the README, the package manifest's scripts, and any CONTRIBUTING
file before writing this, rather than guessing a stack.

**If `checks.your_workflow` already names a workflow, that one is correct.** A
repository with its own CI has it for reasons that are not in front of you. Leave
both alone, and in particular do not add a list beside it: a section
carrying both arms is reported as a configuration error rather than resolved by a
precedence rule, so the change comes back rejected instead of half-applied.

## Deployment

The same two arms, and the same rule — Atomaton's lists, or `deploy.your_workflow`,
never both. Here there are three lists, one per event that ships:

```yaml
deploy:
  on_merge:
    - name: staging
      branches: [develop]
      commands: ["./scripts/deploy.sh staging"]
  on_tag:
    - name: production
      tags: ["v*"]
      branches: [main]
      commands: ["./scripts/deploy.sh prod"]
  on_demand:
    - name: rollback
      commands: ["./scripts/rollback.sh"]
```

`tags` exists in `on_tag` and is required there. `branches` exists in both `on_merge`
and `on_tag`, meaning the same thing in each — which branch's reviewed content this
deployment ships — and omitting it means the default branch. A pattern is a literal
or a prefix followed by `*`.

A tag names a COMMIT, not a branch, so `on_tag`'s `branches` is what keeps a tag on
an unreviewed commit from deploying. `on_demand` entries answer to no event and run
only when named: `gh workflow run atomaton-deploy.yml -f target=rollback`.

Deployments run one at a time, in declared order, and the first failure stops the
rest. `$ATOMATON_DEPLOY_TARGET` holds the entry's name inside its commands.

**A branch named in `branches` must require a pull request**, in either list,
through a ruleset covering it. The run is refused otherwise: a branch anyone can
push to is a deployment anyone can run, with its credentials, on a commit nobody
read.

The shipped ruleset covers the default branch and nothing else, so writing
`branches: [develop]` means adding a ruleset for `develop` as well. That is a
repository setting rather than a file, so say so rather than trying to write it.

## Credentials

Never write a credential into `config.yaml` or into a command. Both are committed
in plain text.

A secret is added to the repository by a person, and then *named* in the list for
the place that needs it:

```yaml
checks:
  from_default_branch:
    - name: cloud-names
      secrets: ["AWS_ROLE_ARN"]
      commands: ["./scripts/check-env-names.sh \"$ATOMATON_PR_TREE\""]
deploy:
  on_tag:
    - name: production
      tags: ["v*"]
      secrets: ["AWS_ROLE_ARN"]
      commands: ["./scripts/deploy.sh prod"]
```

It arrives as an environment variable under that name, in that job and no other.
`tools.secrets` is separate on purpose and must not be merged with these: it is the
only list that enters the agent's own environment.

**`checks.from_pull_request` has no `secrets` key, and cannot.** Those commands are
the pull request's own and it may rewrite them, so a credential named beside one is
one the change being judged can read. A check that needs a credential goes in
`checks.from_default_branch`, whose commands come from the default branch and which
is handed the pull request as a path at `$ATOMATON_PR_TREE`.

**`tools.secrets` needs a second step, and the others do not.** Naming a secret
there authorises the run to hold it; it does not deliver it to any tool. The tool
that needs it must also name it in its own `env`, which is written under
`tools.servers` in the same file:

```yaml
tools:
  secrets: ["SLACK_TOKEN"]
  servers:
    slack:
      command: mcp-server-slack
      env:
        SLACK_TOKEN: "${SLACK_TOKEN}"
```

`tools.servers` is empty in a fresh config and is **additive**: it holds servers a
project adds, and overrides of the ones Atomaton ships. `slack` above is an addition,
so it declares the server in full, starting with the `command` that starts it.

**To route a credential to a server Atomaton ships** — `shell`, `github`, `web`,
`search`, `atomaton`, `atomaton_env`, `files`, `files_readonly` — write its
name with an `env` and nothing else. A shipped name is merged field by field, so
the command, the hooks and the timeout stay as they ship:

```yaml
tools:
  servers:
    <the shipped server's name>:
      env:
        API_TOKEN: "${API_TOKEN}"
```

Do not reconstruct the rest of a shipped entry to do this. You cannot read it in
`config.yaml` — it is not there — and a copied `command` or `args` freezes that
server at today's values, so the next upgrade moves nothing you pasted.

A reference, never a value. Every tool that does not name it — including `shell` —
cannot see it, and that is deliberate rather than a gap to fix. If a tool reports
a missing credential, the question is whether that server's `env` names it: for a
shipped server, an empty `tools.servers` means it was never routed, and that is
the answer rather than a sign something is missing from the file.

`config.yaml` is the only place this goes. There is no tools file in the
repository: the one `atoma` is handed is written at the start of each run, from
the shipped servers and whatever `tools.servers` adds, and deleted with the
runner. Routing a credential anywhere else produces a tool that never receives it,
with nothing reporting why.

`checks` and `deploy` need no routing step: their commands run in a workflow of
their own rather than beside an agent.

**Do not invent a secret name and hope.** If a deployment needs a credential you
cannot see, say so in your report and name exactly which one — a person adds it
and tells you what they called it. A guessed name produces a run that warns, then
fails somewhere unrelated.

**A name you add does not take effect until it is merged.** These lists are read
from the default branch, not from the branch a run is working on, so a credential
you declare will not be present in the run reviewing your own pull request. That
is intended. Do not conclude the mechanism is broken and work around it, and do
not try to test it by reading the value — say in your report which secret the
work now needs.

Prefer no credential at all where the platform allows it. `atomaton-deploy.yml`
declares `id-token: write`, so a cloud provider's OIDC login is available and is
better than any long-lived key.

## What commands cannot express

Reach for a person, not a workaround, when you need:

- a job's `permissions` beyond what the shipped workflows declare. Checks get
  `contents: read` and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` in `GH_TOKEN`, so `gh` works. Deployments
  get `contents: write` and `id-token: write`, so cutting a release and an OIDC
  login both work
- a deployment approval gate (`environment:`) — `environment:` takes no
  expression, so configuration cannot reach it
- a trigger outside merge, tag and manual dispatch — schedules in particular
  cannot come from configuration
- GitHub's own artifact store or cache

Most limits people assume are here are not. Service containers work through
`docker run`. A matrix works as a loop, losing only parallelism. Those are
commands; write them.

## The required check

If a ruleset requires a status check, its `context` must equal the job name that
produces it. `.github/atomaton/rulesets/main.json` ships already matched to
`atomaton-check.yml`. **Do not edit either side to make them agree** — a mismatch
does not fail a pull request, it leaves it waiting forever on a check that will
never report, and no amount of re-running fixes it. If they appear mismatched,
report it.

## Finishing

Changing `.github/atomaton/config.yaml` is a governed change: you may write it and
open the pull request, and a person merges it. That is expected, not an
obstruction. Say plainly in the pull request what will now run, on which events,
and which secrets a person still has to add.

{"title": "Separate a hand-off from a chain that continues elsewhere (#449)", "body": "Closes #449.

## The defect

A merged pull request stayed permanently readable as "running". The post-merge dispatch of the issue a pull request delivers is written onto the pull request's own thread, and the runner recorded it as `atomaton:ended=handoff` — a promise that the next agent runs **here**, on a node nothing can ever run on again. Every reader of that tag inherited the lie. Measured on #442: closing a parent whose children had all merged hours before announced stopping runs on #445 and #446, which had had no run since merging.

## The fix: two facts, two signals

`handed-off` keeps its meaning — a directive names the next agent **on this node**. The other fact gets its own signal:

- `TurnEnding.continues?: true` — a run started on **another** node, so "nothing runs next" is not true even though this node handed back.
- `endingOf` returns `finished` / `no-report` **plus** `continues` when a dispatch went elsewhere; a directive still produces `handed-off`.
- `shouldReleaseGuard` returns `false` for `continues` — the label behaviour is deliberately unchanged, because `shouldReleaseGuard` and the aggregation double signal already read it.
- `completion-mention.ts` suppresses on `chainContinues || ending.continues`, with the `chainContinues` check moved **above** the `no-report` override so a silent chain-continuing run no longer mentions a person.

`atomaton:ended` therefore reads `done` for a chain-continuing run, `handoff` only for a directive.

## Existing data: narrow on `merged`, never on `closed`

`runInFlight(repo, number, { merged })` lets only the claim (`atomaton:took`) count on a merged pull request. Its three call sites pass the flag from the data that already named the node (`pull_request.merged_at`; `state === "MERGED"`; `false` for native links).

The distinction matters in both directions: the run that performs its **own** merge is still in flight while it finishes, so a stop still reaches it; and an issue **closed** by the run working it still holds that run — which is why the narrowing is on `merged` and not on "closed", pinned by the existing *"a closed issue keeps the wider answer"* test.

## `stop_on_close`

`stopOnCloseNotice(number, running)` has two receipts. `stopOnCloseBody` takes an options object `{ number, rootRunning, closed, stopped }` and writes `stop=requested` only when the root itself is running — on a parent with no run of its own the tag requests nothing, and with this defect it was posted on every close of a parent that had ever merged a pull request. A descendant that *is* running gets its tag on its own node.

Closing a parent whose only children are merged pull requests now produces neither "Runs were going on …" nor `stop=requested`.

## Deliberately unchanged

The ops-log `dispatch` op and the runner's `chain_continues` output are untouched: they are the "a run started somewhere" signal, and the mention-suppressing intent of `chain_continues` is preserved. No `.wac.ts` edit is needed — no workflow step reads `turn-ending.ended` (verified).

## Tests

Pinned with the fake `gh`, as the issue requires:

- **merged-PR handoff is not in flight** — `thread.test.ts`, `describe("on a merged pull request")`, plus the unmerged and closed cases kept green;
- **close of a parent with merged PRs is silent** — `stop_on_close.test.ts`, both alone and alongside an open sub-issue that *does* need closing;
- **root receipt wording** — `closed-target.test.ts` idle-root receipt, and the idle-root/running-child case split across root and child;
- **genuinely running work is still stopped** — the existing cases, still passing;
- plus the tag itself in `post_result_comment.test.ts` (`ended=done`, not `handoff`, for a chain-continuing run; `handoff` for a directive) and `decide_turn_ending.test.ts` (`ended` is `finished` while the guard is still held).

The three tests that pinned the wrong behaviour were updated deliberately: `mcp.test.ts` (docstring; the ops-log assertion is still correct and unchanged), `decide_turn_ending.test.ts`, and the result-comment mention case.
